cls: Selective relaxant binding agent - modified gamma-cyclodextrin
quick: 2 or 4 mg/kg IV by depth of block; 16 mg/kg for immediate reversal
Not applicable - single IV bolus during anesthesia
Limited data; may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy for 7 days
Likely compatible; minimal oral bioavailability in infant
Avoid in severe impairment (CrCl <30) and dialysis - not recommended
No adjustment for mild-moderate; caution in severe (limited data)
Not relevant in acute perioperative use
Neuromuscular function (TOF), ventilation, heart rate, hypersensitivity
summary: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin that rapidly reverses neuromuscular blockade produced by the aminosteroid agents rocuronium and vecuronium. It encapsulates the blocker in plasma, removing it from the neuromuscular junction, and is given as a single weight-based IV bolus selected by the depth of block (2, 4, or 16 mg/kg). Key risks are anaphylaxis and marked bradycardia (occasionally cardiac arrest). It also reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives for 7 days. It is not recommended in severe renal impairment.
indications: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium bromide in adults and pediatric patients undergoing surgery
Reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by vecuronium bromide in adults and pediatric patients undergoing surgery

dosage.d: 2 mg/kg IV when recovery has reached reappearance of the second twitch (T2) on TOF
dosage.n: Dose based on actual body weight; monitor with TOF

dosage.d: 4 mg/kg IV when recovery has reached 1-2 post-tetanic counts with no TOF twitches
16 mg/kg IV given ~3 minutes after a rocuronium intubating dose
dosage.n: For urgent reversal soon after administration

dosage.d: 2 mg/kg IV at reappearance of T2

admin: Administer as a single IV bolus injection based on actual body weight
Use neuromuscular (train-of-four) monitoring to choose the dose by depth of block and to confirm recovery
Provide ventilatory support until adequate spontaneous breathing and airway control return
If neuromuscular blockade recurs, treat with re-dosing and continued ventilation; have resuscitation drugs (including atropine) available
moa: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin that forms a tight 1:1 inclusion complex with the aminosteroid neuromuscular blockers rocuronium and (less avidly) vecuronium in plasma. This lowers the free drug available to bind nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction, creating a concentration gradient that draws the blocker away from the junction and rapidly reverses paralysis. The complex is then eliminated renally.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to sugammadex or any component
relative: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min), including dialysis - use not recommended
Coagulopathy / patients on anticoagulants (transient prolongation of coagulation tests)
Use of hormonal contraceptives (reduced efficacy for 7 days)

preg: There are no adequate clinical data in pregnant women; animal studies did not show malformations. Importantly, sugammadex can bind progestogens and may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives - exposure is equivalent to missing one daily dose, so backup non-hormonal contraception is needed for 7 days.
lact: Limited data. Sugammadex has low oral bioavailability, so absorption by a breastfed infant is expected to be minimal; it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding after recovery from anesthesia.
renal: Sugammadex and the sugammadex-rocuronium complex are eliminated renally. Use is not recommended in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min), including patients requiring dialysis, due to lack of supporting safety data and impaired clearance.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment or hepatic disease accompanied by coagulopathy, as data are limited and elimination may be affected.

major: Hormonal contraceptives - sugammadex binds progestogen, reducing efficacy for 7 days (equivalent to a missed dose); advise additional non-hormonal contraception
moderate: Toremifene (high affinity for sugammadex; may delay recovery from blockade)
Fusidic acid (displacement interaction; may cause recurrence of blockade)
minor: Re-administration of rocuronium/vecuronium soon after reversal requires specific waiting times or alternative (non-steroidal) blockers
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant to acute perioperative use
interactions.diagnostics: Transiently prolongs aPTT and PT/INR by up to ~1 hour; can interfere with some progesterone assays

serious: Anaphylaxis / hypersensitivity reactions (including in patients with no prior exposure)
Marked bradycardia, occasionally progressing to cardiac arrest
rare: Coagulation parameter prolongation with bleeding concern
emergency: Severe bradycardia or cardiac arrest within minutes of administration

monitoring: Neuromuscular function with train-of-four monitoring before and after reversal
Ventilation and airway protection until full recovery
Heart rate and rhythm (watch for bradycardia in the minutes after dosing)
counsel: Given by your anesthesia team at the end of surgery to reverse muscle relaxants
If you use hormonal birth control, it may not work for 7 days - use a backup non-hormonal method (oral) or for 7 days (non-oral)
Tell your team about any previous reaction to this drug or muscle relaxants
Rarely it can cause a slow heart rate or allergic reaction, which staff are prepared to treat
Breathing is supported until your strength fully returns
pk: Very rapid - recovery to TOF ratio >=0.9 typically within ~2-3 minutes
Immediate plasma concentration after IV bolus
Single dose reverses blockade for the procedure; re-dose if recurrence
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: Reverses only aminosteroid blockers (rocuronium, vecuronium) - it does NOT reverse benzylisoquinolinium agents such as atracurium or cisatracurium
Choose the dose (2, 4, or 16 mg/kg) by the measured depth of block, using actual body weight
Reduces hormonal contraceptive efficacy for 7 days - counsel on backup contraception
Watch for marked bradycardia and anaphylaxis (which can occur even on first exposure); not recommended if CrCl <30 mL/min
missed: Not applicable - sugammadex is a single intraoperative reversal dose given by the anesthesia provider, not a scheduled self-administered medication.
overdose: Accidental overdose (reported up to 40 mg/kg) was tolerated without significant effects. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive. Sugammadex can be removed by hemodialysis using a high-flux filter (concentrations reduced by about 70% over a 3-6 hour session).
